title: Surgical canary quarantine and tenant-facing communication playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a compact, operator-friendly playbook for surgical containment of model rollout regressions discovered during canary or early-stage ramp. This ticket focuses on cross-environment coordination (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with clear tenant-safety actions, rapid mitigations, and customer communication templates.

Scope:
- Define automated and manual steps for quarantining a canary cohort (tenant slice) without broadly impacting healthy traffic.
- Provide environment-specific constraints and actions for Hosted (fast rollback/pin), Dedicated (reserved pools + tenant routing), and Private (customer-managed control plane + on-prem constraints).
- Create communication templates and escalation handoffs for Support, Solutions, and Account teams.
- Add verification checks, telemetry queries, and post-incident follow-up tasks to ensure regression does not recur.

High-level approach and decisions made so far:
1) Quarantine model variant per-tenant slice using runtime routing tags (decision): use dynamic tag-based routing to divert affected requests to a known-good model or fallback variant. This minimizes global blast radius. Tradeoff: requires up-to-date tag mapping in Dedicated and Private where tenant networking may be opaque.
2) Progressive traffic fencing (decision): implement 3-tier fencing: (A) Immediate canary quarantine (0-1 min), (B) Slice drain + warm fallback (1-10 min), (C) Controlled rollback/pin at region level (10-60 min).
3) Hotpatch vs rollback (decision): prefer hotpatch to restore functional behavior when feasible; otherwise perform a fast binary rollback. Hotpatch requires QA approval and may be slower for Private deployments.

Environment-specific notes:
- Hosted: can pin model version at edge and flip routing rules via control plane. Use auto-fallback to CPU-quantized variant if GPU capacity missing. Link to automation: https://github.com/redwood/runtime-ops/tree/main/automations/canary-quarantine
- Dedicated: use tenant-to-pool mapping to isolate impact. If affected pool is dedicated to an account, engage Account Manager and enable temporary extra capacity if rollback increases cost. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/pools
- Private: limited remote control. Provide documented remediation checklist for on-prem operators and include signed playbook bundle that customer can apply. Store artifacts in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-canary-playbook

Runbook and verification:
- Primary runbook: internal/runbooks/canary-quarantine.md (adds step-by-step commands and telemetry queries).
- Key SLO checks: token latency P95, error-rate by tenant, divergence from baseline embedding similarity.
- Telemetry queries (Grafana/Prometheus): queries are included in the runbook and linked dashboards.

Communication plan:
- T=0 internal: Pager alert -> Ops oncall + Responsible engineer -> create incident channel (#inc-<key>).
- T=5 min: Notify affected customers (templated) with current mitigation and ETA for next update. Use Support template 1 (customer-visible) and Solutions template 2 (detailed). Templates stored: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Customer+Escalation+Templates
- T=30 min: Provide technical postmortem draft to Solutions and AMs for impacted customers.

Artifacts and links:
- Automation repo: https://github.com/redwood/runtime-ops/pull/1942 (quarantine orchestration PR).
- Canary dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/CanaryOverview
- Incident runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/123456789/canary-quarantine-playbook
- Customer communication templates: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/234567890/escalation-templates

Open risks and tradeoffs:
- Private deployments may not accept hotpatches due to compliance; ensure playbooks include signed checksums and offline instructions.
- Rolling back large models in Dedicated can spike costs as traffic shifts to alternative pools; include cost guardrails.
- Automated fencing needs accurate tenant-to-slice tagging; include verification CI that exercises tagging on every rollout.

Deliverables:
- Finalized runbook (MD) with commands and telemetry queries.
- Automation scripts for Hosted/Dedicated fencing and a customer-friendly bundle for Private.
- Communication templates and a short training slide deck for oncall and Solutions.

Success criteria (short-term):
- A canary incident is contained to the affected slice in >=90% of simulated drills.
- Mean time to mitigation reduced by 40% in runbook drills.

Next steps:
- Finish automation PR review and merge: runtime-ops PR #1942 (owner: @mruiz).
- Run 3 simulated drills (hosted, dedicated, private) with SRE and Solutions by 2026-03-18.
- Coordinate with Security to confirm playbook is safe for Private customers by 2026-03-15.
